To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have established a new tick cell culture system, isolated two tick strains of the human granulocytotrophic ehrlichia from an infected horse, and dog, and have established a human isolate of the HGE from the human cell line, HL60, and that these strains are infectious for tick cell cultures.
the human HGE agent can infect and multiply within tick cell culture.
the HGE agent is infectious for tick cells and that tick cell culture is a useful model for the study of the ehrlichial developmental cycle in ticks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the HGE pathogen within the vector tick, a critical step for the transmission of this disease.
the development of the HGE organism within the tick vector, which has not been described before.
the development of the HGE organism in tick cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HGE agent can be transmitted by ticks, and that tick cells are permissive to ehrlichial infection and replication.

the HGE agent is infectious for tick cells and replicates in them, but whether the tick cells are the only reservoir of the HGE agents in the tick or whether the HGE agent replicates in other tick cells and tissues has yet to be determined.

the ehrlichias in the vector undergo a developmental cycle in which they are ingested and replicated, and then, as they become more compact, they are shed into the environment, where they are ingested by the mammalian host.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HGE agent has a life cycle in ticks that is similar to that in human neutrophils.
the ehrlichia can be transmitted from the horse or dog to the vector and that the vector can transmit it back to the horse or dog.
the HGE agent can be cultured directly in vector tick cells and undergoes a developmental cycle that is similar to that of the agent of bovine granulocytic E. ruminantium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HGE agent has a life cycle in tick cell layers that includes adherence, internalization, replication, and cell-to-cell transmission.
the HGE agent can infect tick cells and replicate to high titers, and that this may be an important step in the transmission of the HGE agents to mammalian hosts.
we have established tick cell culture systems that are useful for studying HGE agent biology, which will be important for vaccine development.
